text: Given the MCP server has registered this change, When FastMCP list_tools() is called, Then mspbotsagent_get_usage_overview exists, its annotations have readOnlyHint set to true, and its set of required parameters is empty
Given an upstream response containing a debug field, When it is passed to the shaping function, Then the return value has no debug, and every other top-level field equals the upstream one

Given a breakdown with so many rows that the serialized output exceeds _json.MAX_CHARS, When it is passed to the shaping function, Then the return value carries breakdownReturned (the actual row count) and breakdownTruncatedByToolOutput=true, and breakdownTotal is still the upstream original value, so the two are distinguishable

Given the upstream returns spendUnavailable=true and spendTruncated=true, When it is passed to the shaping function, Then these two booleans appear as-is in the return value, with values not rewritten

Given client_factory returns None (no credentials), When the tool is called, Then it returns a not_configured error envelope; Given the upstream raises an AgentError with 401, Then it returns the envelope mapped by to_envelope(), not the wrapper's own generic error

Given a valid platform token, When the tool is called without any parameters, Then the returned JSON matches the response of a direct curl GET /api/usage/overview on every top-level field (except debug)
steps: Get the platform JWT of a test tenant (take it from browser devtools, do not write it to disk)
Call mspbotsagent_get_usage_overview with no parameters through an MCP client (or check_tool_call in test/src/mcp_probe.py) and save the return value

Compare the two JSON documents field by field: range / startDate / endDate / totalSpend / threads / runs / agents / daily / breakdown / breakdownTotal / page / pageSize / sortBy / sortOrder / timeZone / spendUnavailable / spendTruncated
Confirm that the tool return value has no debug
expect: Every top-level field is equal except debug; page=1, pageSize=10, sortBy=cost, sortOrder=desc, range=7d
evidence: 2026-09-03 live (agent.mspbots.ai, Asia/Shanghai tenant): compared with the front end's own /api/usage/overview response, the top-level fields returned by the tool have missing=[] extra=[], debug is stripped, and the six stable fields range/page/pageSize/sortBy/sortOrder/timeZone are equal one by one (7d/1/10/cost/desc/Asia/Shanghai). breakdownTotal=453, tool output 2820 characters. Evidence file scratchpad/live_evidence.json, cases.TC6

text: Given the same token, When range / page / pageSize / sortBy / sortOrder / sopId / source are passed one at a time, Then each is forwarded and the result visibly changes; when invalid values are passed there is no error and it falls back to the server default
steps: range=30d: confirm the response has range=30d and startDate moves earlier accordingly
page=2 and pageSize=1: confirm breakdown has only 1 row and it differs from the row on page=1
sortBy=runs + sortOrder=asc: confirm the ordering of breakdown changes accordingly
sopId=<a real SOP id>: confirm agents/breakdownTotal narrow down to that agent
source=task and source=chat: confirm runs changes while totalSpend stays the same
Three invalid values: range=xx, sopId=-1, sortBy=nope - confirm one by one that there is no error and the response falls back to 7d / no sopId / cost
expect: In the first five steps the result visibly changes at each step; in the sixth step all three invalid values return 200 with fields falling back to defaults, and there is no error envelope
evidence: 2026-09-03 live: range=30d changed startDate; page=2&pageSize=1 returned a different sopId than page=1; sortBy=runs gave different orders for asc/desc; sopId=<real id> narrowed breakdownTotal; source: all=303 task=7 chat=286, with totalSpend unchanged (consistent with the ticket's "only affects run counts"). Invalid values: range=xx->7d, sortBy=nope->cost, sopId=-1 all returned 200 with no error envelope. The httpx log shows that the query of each request carried only the one parameter passed and unpassed ones did not appear - proving the drop semantics of _clean_params take effect. Evidence cases.TC7

text: Given the target deployment is confirmed to contain mb-platform-agent commit 08745928, When the tool is called, Then every row of breakdown has createdBy (email or UUID) and createdAt (ISO), and for rows with deleted=true both are null
steps: First confirm that the deployed version contains 08745928: run git branch --contains 08745928 on mb-platform-agent, confirm it is on the branch corresponding to the target environment (release-aks or INT), and note how it was confirmed
Call the tool and take breakdown
Check that every row has both createdBy and createdAt keys (values may be null)
Find one row whose createdBy is an email and one whose is a UUID (if both can be found), and record one example of each
Increase pageSize or page through to find a row with deleted=true, and confirm both its createdBy and createdAt are null
expect: Every row contains these two keys; for rows with deleted=true both are null. If the deployment does not contain 08745928, both keys are missing altogether - in that case record blocked and state the deployed version, and do not judge it as an implementation omission
evidence: 2026-09-03 live (pageSize=1000, tenant breakdownTotal=453): 99 rows returned, all containing both createdBy and createdAt keys; of these 34 rows have emails, 10 rows are non-email (UUID fallback), 55 rows are null; 55 archived (deleted=true) rows have both fields null. Precondition verified: 08745928 was measured via git merge-base --is-ancestor to be on mb-platform-agent's origin/release-aks and origin/INT. Evidence cases.TC8
notes: The precondition of this case is OQ-3. If the deployed version cannot be confirmed, record blocked; do not change the case to accommodate it
